lead.headline: Anthropic's Debut Can't Stop a Global AI Sell-Off: Dow Sheds 1,101 Points and Asia Plunges
lead.dek: ANT closed 17% above its $83 issue price, but the S&P 500 fell 2% for a sixth straight loss; on Friday the Nikkei and Kospi dropped more than 4% and Taiwan about 6%.
body: The largest IPO on record arrived on a day the market wanted to sell. Anthropic's shares first traded at $111.50 just before noon in New York on Thursday, touched about $115 and then faded to close at $97.17, still about 17% above the $83 offer price. As ANT opened, the main indices slid to their lows, and they never recovered: the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, its first close below 50,000 since June. The S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,175.83, its sixth losing session in a row, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% to 23,879.20.

The selling went well beyond technology, with industrials down about 2.6%, but AI names led it. Nvidia fell 3.3% to $145.98 on volume nearly double its three-month average, AMD sank 7.7%, CoreWeave 6.1% and Nebius 9.4%, while Alphabet reversed an early 4% gain to end down about 3.5% and Amazon lost 3.9%. Investors were weighing a hawkish Federal Reserve that is all but certain to raise rates on 9 December, a weak Philadelphia Fed survey, fresh legal pressure on Nvidia after Jensen Huang's exit, and new US limits on Chinese access to AI chips. The VIX jumped about 16% to 28.44 after nearing 29 intraday, its highest since March.

Asia took the hit on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 was down about 4.5% in morning trade, with SoftBank Group, Kioxia and Ibiden each off more than 10%, while South Korea's Kospi fell about 4.7% and Taiwan's Taiex nearly 6%, a day after a 4.4% slide. The Hang Seng dropped as much as 2%, leaving it roughly 20% below its January peak, close to a bear market. US index futures were lower again in Asian hours, by 0.1% to 0.7% depending on the contract and the time quoted.

Europe had closed before the worst of the US slide but still fell about 0.9% on the STOXX 600, DAX and FTSE 100. India was the exception on Thursday, with the Sensex up 1.2% on autos and record foreign inflows, though GIFT Nifty pointed to a lower open on Friday.

impact.title: What it means for markets
points: The AI complex is now trading on financing and policy risk rather than earnings: Nvidia beat its own guidance last week yet is down sharply since Huang's departure, and Asian chip and supply-chain names carry the most beta.
A sixth straight S&P 500 loss with the VIX near 29 and the Fed set to hike in December leaves little support from rates; the 10-year yield sits around 5.05%-5.07%.
Anthropic holding above its issue price matters for the IPO pipeline, but the after-hours dip to about $92.60 shows how thin the cushion is; index funds cannot buy yet.
Havens are not working the usual way: gold is at a 14-month low and bitcoin near $63,000, while the dollar and the yen near 160 dominate FX.

read.title: The Ledger's Read
paragraphs: Thursday was supposed to be the AI trade's vindication. Anthropic sold $81 billion of stock above its range and still closed 17% higher on day one, yet the S&P 500 fell 2% for a sixth straight loss and the Dow lost more than 1,100 points. The message is that a successful listing does not solve the sector's problems: Nvidia is leaderless and under investigation, Washington is tightening the rules on who can use American chips, and the capital spending that powered the rally now has to be financed at 5% long-term yields. Friday's 4%-6% falls in Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei show where that doubt bites hardest, in the hardware supply chain.

Rates are the other half of the story. Futures price a December Fed hike almost fully, with a half-point move a live minority view, and the ECB and Bank of Japan are both expected to hike next month. In that setting the usual shelters are failing: gold is at a 14-month low, bitcoin is down a fifth in November, and only the dollar and short-dated cash are paying. Oil is the exception that cuts both ways; a still-closed Hormuz and fresh attacks on Gulf targets keep Brent near $92 even as US stockpiles build and the summit in Shenzhen promises more fuel.

What to watch: whether US stocks can stop the losing streak before next week's PCE data, how Lagarde frames the path after December this morning, and whether Asia's Friday slide spills into Europe's open. India, carried by record foreign inflows, is the market to watch for whether money rotates away from AI-heavy Asia rather than leaving the region.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin Sign a Four-Point 'Peace Declaration' That Leaves Out Ukraine and Iran
stories.summary: The first three-way meeting of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders lasted about 80 minutes on Thursday at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC. Their joint declaration covered UN reform, nuclear risk, immunity for officials and a pledge to raise the production and supply of refined petroleum products, but set no targets or timelines and did not mention Ukraine, Iran or the Strait of Hormuz. There was no ceasefire in either war and no commitment to cut warheads. Xi called the talks positive and fruitful, according to Xinhua.
stories.market: The fuel-supply pledge added to downward pressure on product prices, but without a Hormuz or Ukraine breakthrough the war premiums in oil, gas and shipping remain; defence stocks lost a potential catalyst for de-escalation.

body: Beyond the nuclear language, which reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won, the declaration said the International Criminal Court should not abuse its jurisdiction. No regular trilateral format was announced.

Trump and Putin also discussed Ukraine for about 40 minutes in a separate meeting. Iran had launched drone and missile strikes on Bahrain and Kuwait on 18 November, its first in about two months, shortly before the summit.

stories.headline: Iran War, Day 266: Tanker Attacks Multiply in Hormuz While Trump Signals No Rush to Strike
stories.summary: Attacks on merchant ships around the Strait of Hormuz have stepped up: the Joint Maritime Information Center logged five tanker attacks and two armed-skiff approaches in its update covering to 19 November, four of them in the strait, and kept the threat level at 'severe'. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 19 November that two more supertankers carrying over 4 million barrels hit mines on an 'unauthorised route'; the claim is unverified and JMIC lists the earlier hits as unknown projectiles. A US official says Iran has begun using anti-ship cruise missiles, yet also says a record 28 million barrels passed through the strait on 18 November. Reports say Israel is pressing for a four-to-seven-day US campaign, but Trump said he is 'not rushing' and pointed to after 1 January; the Pentagon puts the war's cost above $48bn since late February.
stories.market: Brent settled flat at $91.98 on 19 November, about 20% lower this month, as unverified mine claims were offset by a 3.4m-barrel US crude build and surplus forecasts; WTI's $83.21 was its lowest close since 26 August. Tanker owners, marine war-risk insurers, Gulf equities and Asian LNG buyers carry the most direct exposure.

body: The war that began with US and Israeli strikes on 28 February has no ceasefire, and Iran still requires ships to obtain its approval to use the strait, warning on 19 November that tankers cooperating with the US military will be 'dealt with decisively'. The US keeps a naval blockade of Iranian ports, and talks remain stalled despite a June memorandum of understanding.

The latest Joint Maritime Information Center update, covering 1 March to 19 November, records the LPG carrier Tara Gas hit twice north of Khasab, Oman, on 16-17 November with one crew member missing, and the Navig8 Messi struck on 17 November with one missing and 11 injured according to ADNOC. Other tankers were hit on 16 and 18 November. Iran says the vessels struck mines; no party has claimed responsibility.

On the US side, three carrier strike groups are in the Central Command area since the USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived on 15 November, and the amphibious ship USS Makin Island is heading to the region, expected in about ten days. Bloomberg and The New York Times reported on 19 November that further strikes are growing more likely, but Trump told Israel's Channel 12 he could wait until after the new year. He also said, without giving evidence, that Iran may be looking at chemical or biological weapons; Iran's foreign ministry called the allegation fraudulent.

The conflict is spilling across the region: Bahrain and Kuwait intercepted Iranian drones and missiles after US strikes on Qeshm Island on 17 November, and Iraqi forces were due on 20 November to set up a command post in Jurf al-Sakhar, a Kataib Hezbollah stronghold south of Baghdad accused of oil smuggling. The International Energy Agency has called the Hormuz crisis the largest threat to energy security in history.

For markets the paradox is that flows appear to be improving even as attacks rise. Brent closed at $91.98 on 19 November against $117.64 on 30 October; European diesel futures touched a three-month low the same day, and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Washington was considering more oil and diesel exports to Europe.

stories.headline: Houthi Missiles Hit Riyadh's Financial District as Fighters Close In on Aden
stories.summary: A Houthi missile attack on Riyadh on 19 November left debris that visibly damaged the Public Investment Fund tower in the King Abdullah Financial District; Saudi authorities reported no injuries. The Houthis also claimed strikes on the Sadaf petrochemical complex in Jubail and on King Khalid airport, claims that could not be verified. On the ground, after government forces gave up the Bab el-Mandeb shore on 15 November, the Houthis held the coast to Khor Umairah, about 60 miles west of Aden, as of 18 November. The Saudi-led coalition said it hit 60 Houthi targets on 17 November.
stories.market: With Hormuz disrupted, the Red Sea is Saudi Arabia's main export outlet: the East-West pipeline to Yanbu carries about 4m barrels a day and was struck on 9 November, so threats to the corridor and to Riyadh itself bear on Saudi equities, the kingdom's deficit and freight. Egypt's Suez revenue had just recovered to $724m in October, the highest since 2023.

body: The Houthis said they targeted Riyadh at dawn and in the evening on 19 November in retaliation for Saudi strikes; the coalition said it intercepted missiles over the south overnight. The Houthi-run health ministry said air strikes killed 15 people in Mokha and Taiz province, blaming Saudi-backed forces.

The ground war has turned toward Aden. Government forces described their 15 November pullback from Dhubab as a redeployment; by 18 November Houthi fighters were about 15 miles from government lines at Qa'wa and inland had reached the al-Khiraz camp, about 37 miles from the city. The Houthis claim 7,100 square kilometres of Lahij and Taiz, which is unconfirmed.

Shipping has adapted unevenly. Some vessels now seek seven-day transit permits from a Houthi coordination centre, while Saudi- and Israeli-linked ships still avoid the southern Red Sea. The Joint War Committee has left its listed area unchanged. Suez traffic was recovering before the latest offensive: Ocean Network Express sent its first ship through in nearly three years on 15 November, and Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd plan more Asia-Europe returns between December and January.

Fiscal strain is visible on both sides of the sea. Aramco output was 8.7m barrels a day in the third quarter against 10.8m a year earlier, and Saudi Arabia's nine-month deficit reached SAR 244.3bn against SAR 165.4bn budgeted for the whole year. Egypt's IMF programme expires on 15 December with about $2.3bn still to be released.

stories.headline: Israel Ends Two-Day Central Gaza Push, Strikes Beqaa Again
stories.summary: The Israeli army said on 19 November it had completed a ground operation with tanks near the Bureij and Nuseirat camps in central Gaza, beyond the Yellow Line, that began a day earlier; it said the aim was to destroy a tunnel, and Hamas called it a blatant violation. The October 2025 ceasefire formally holds, but more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since it began according to an AFP tally of health ministry data, along with seven Israeli soldiers and a contractor. In Lebanon, Israeli jets struck the entrances to an underground Hezbollah missile site near Janta in the Beqaa Valley on the evening of 19 November, the second strike in eastern Lebanon in days. The UN peacekeeping mission UNIFIL is due to end on 31 December.
stories.market: These fronts reach markets mainly through regional risk premia: Israeli assets and the shekel, Lebanese debt and East Mediterranean gas. A breakdown of the Gaza or Lebanon truce would add to the Gulf risk already in oil prices.

body: Israel's civil affairs body said Palestinians could again move freely in the targeted areas of central Gaza after the operation ended, and that the Salah al-Din road had reopened. A day earlier the board overseeing the US peace plan warned that both Israel and Hamas were failing to meet their commitments.

In Lebanon, the Israeli military said it had seen Hezbollah operatives returning to the Janta facility and struck its entrances to stop it being rebuilt; Lebanese media reported several strikes and no immediate casualties. On 16 November Israel had hit a weapons shipment from Syria bound for Hezbollah.

Hezbollah joined the war on Iran on 2 March, prompting an Israeli air and ground campaign. An agreement to end that round was reached in June, under which Israel would withdraw from parts of the south as the Lebanese army deploys, conditional on Hezbollah disarming; Hezbollah's refusal has stalled the process, and Israel still holds a buffer zone about 10 km deep.
The scheduled end of UNIFIL on 31 December adds a deadline: the Security Council reaffirmed support for the mission this week but did not say whether that extends past the end of the year.

stories.headline: US Envoys Join Europe in Berlin as Ukraine's Drones Cut Russian Refining by 45%
stories.summary: Nearly 40 delegations met in Berlin on 19 November for the largest Coalition of the Willing meeting so far, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner present and Trump joining by phone. Kushner said Trump is open to security guarantees for Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5 and that Russia has agreed to multilateral talks including Europe; Putin instead proposed that European envoys travel to Moscow first. On the ground, Russia launched 98 drones and Oniks missiles overnight into 19 November, cutting power to 99 settlements in Mykolaiv region, while Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge rail section for the third time in a week. Reuters industry sources say Ukrainian strikes have cut Russian refinery runs by about 45% since late October.
stories.market: Lost Russian refining supports diesel cracks, yet European diesel futures fell to a three-month low on 19 November on surplus expectations and US export talk. European defence stocks trade on the peace track; Dutch TTF gas, near €86/MWh on 17 November with EU storage only about 70% full, is more exposed to Hormuz LNG and the cold snap forecast from 20 November.

body: Germany, France, Britain and Ukraine said in a joint statement after the Berlin meeting that Russia cannot outlast their support, and Chancellor Merz said a 'Yalta' format would not bring peace. Kushner said Trump left his Shenzhen meeting with Putin and Xi convinced peace is achievable; Zelensky said it was unclear how Article 5-style guarantees would work. The Kremlin said it had not agreed to repeat last week's Abu Dhabi format with Europeans present.

Ukraine's deep-strike campaign continued: the General Staff confirmed hits on two Krasnodar refineries on 17 November, and drones reportedly set the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Tatarstan ablaze overnight into 19 November, which is unconfirmed by officials. A Flamingo missile strike collapsed a section of the Crimean Bridge on 17 November, and Russia suspended train services after the latest attack.

Russia's winter campaign against Ukraine's energy system went on, with 69 of 98 drones downed or suppressed by morning on 19 November and hits at 18 locations, including energy and industrial sites in Odesa region. The General Staff recorded 211 combat clashes in a day, concentrated on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes.
Ukraine's defence ministry said it will be able to pay for US weapons through the PURL mechanism using EU loan funds.

stories.headline: Sudan's Army Pushes Past Al-Khuway Toward the RSF's Kordofan Strongholds
stories.summary: Sudan's army said its troops swept villages around Al-Khuway and north and east of Al-Nuhud and Abu Zabad on 17 November, after taking Al-Saatat, northeast of Abu Zabad, on 16 November; the Rapid Support Forces pulled back from several positions, according to military sources. A local relief committee says the army has retaken eight administrative areas around Al-Khuway, about 100 km from Al-Nuhud. Women's and press groups in Port Sudan on 19 November condemned drone attacks by both sides on populated areas. The UN refugee agency counts about 11.4 million people forcibly displaced by the war.
stories.market: Sudan's war is financed partly by gold from Darfur, so shifts in Kordofan affect gold flows through neighbouring states, trade via Port Sudan and the humanitarian burden on Egypt and Chad.

body: The army describes Abu Zabad as the link between northern and southern West Kordofan, which makes the advance strategically important for any move on the RSF-held towns to the west. All battlefield claims come from army and local sources and have not been independently verified.

The campaign, which began in July to secure the route between Khartoum and El Obeid, accelerated in November. Drones have become the war's dominant weapon on both sides; activists told Radio Dabanga on 19 November that the attacks breach international humanitarian law.
The war, which began in April 2023, has killed tens of thousands of people.

stories.headline: UniCredit and Berlin Strike a Broad Deal on Commerzbank, Clearing the Way for Europe's Biggest Bank Merger
stories.summary: UniCredit and the German government reached broad agreement on the sticking points of UniCredit's €45 billion takeover of Commerzbank, set out in an 18 November letter from chief executive Andrea Orcel to Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil. The combined bank's German arm keeps its headquarters in Frankfurt as a listed entity, Berlin dropped its demand for two supervisory board seats, and UniCredit will add German nationals to its own board. The merged group would hold more than €1.3 trillion of assets. Commerzbank shares slipped about 1.2% to €37.27 on Thursday from a €37.71 close.
stories.market: The deal removes the main political obstacle to a cross-border bank tie-up; the next question is whether Berlin sells its 13.3% stake, which would add supply in Commerzbank shares. Analysts' average target is €42.51.

body: Orcel wrote that UniCredit is prepared to commit to binding principles, and that the terms set the basis for selling the government's stake; Klingbeil's statement made no commitment to sell.

The ECB, the European Commission and the US Federal Reserve have already cleared the transaction. Commerzbank's works council said existing employment contracts stay valid, while Orcel said job cuts would start at the top.
UniCredit shares rose 1.6% and Commerzbank 1.3% in early trade on Thursday before the wider market turned lower.

stories.headline: Barclays Lifts Its STOXX 600 Target to 725 but Turns Underweight on Luxury
stories.summary: Barclays raised its end-2027 target for the STOXX 600 to 725, about 12% above Thursday's mid-morning level of 645, while cutting European luxury stocks to underweight. The call came as the index sat near a three-week low after several days of losses led by miners.
stories.market: A constructive index view paired with a luxury downgrade points investors toward domestic cyclicals and away from China-exposed consumer names such as LVMH, Kering and Richemont.

stories.headline: Record Foreign Buying Tops ₹1 Lakh Crore in November as Goldman Turns Overweight
stories.summary: Foreign portfolio investors have put a record ₹1.08 lakh crore into Indian equities in November through 18 November, according to market round-ups, the strongest month on record. Goldman Sachs upgraded India to overweight with a December 2027 Nifty target of 28,500, about 12% above Thursday's close. Public-sector banks reported a record combined first-half net profit of ₹1.09 lakh crore, up 16.9%.
stories.market: Sustained inflows are supporting the rupee and large-cap banks; Nifty Bank touched 63,000 for the first time on Thursday.

stories.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields Raises ₹2,295 Crore From Anchors as Eldorado Agritech Trims Its IPO
stories.summary: Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields raised ₹2,295 crore from anchor investors including ADIA and LIC before its public offer. Eldorado Agritech cut its IPO to ₹504 crore, with a ₹174 crore fresh issue and a ₹330 crore sale by promoters, and Assetz won SEBI approval to raise about ₹1,200 crore. SEBI also ruled out extending trading hours.
stories.market: A heavy primary pipeline is absorbing part of the record foreign inflow; grey-market premiums on Mahanadi and Crystal Crop are the near-term gauge of demand.

stories.headline: China Holds Lending Rates for an 18th Month as Hong Kong Nears a Bear Market
stories.summary: China left its one-year loan prime rate at 3.0% and the five-year rate at 3.5% on Friday, unchanged for an 18th straight month, according to Trading Economics. Hong Kong's Hang Seng closed down 1.95% at 22,841.62 on Thursday and fell up to 2.1% more on Friday, leaving it about 20% below its January peak. The yuan's central parity was set at 6.7128 per dollar on Thursday and the offshore yuan traded near 6.69 on Friday.
stories.market: With no rate relief, Chinese property developers and banks get no help, while Hong Kong tech is tracking the global AI sell-off; the Hang Seng Tech index fell 2.33% on Thursday.

stories.summary: China and South Korea concluded the second phase of upgrading their free-trade agreement, covering services. Goods trade between them reached $440.9 billion in the first ten months of the year, up 63.7%.
stories.market: Wider services access helps Korean travel, entertainment and consumer stocks, though Friday's chip-led Kospi slide overwhelmed any lift.

stories.headline: Washington Approved 879,000 AI Chips for China in Six Months, House Data Show
stories.summary: The House Foreign Affairs Committee released licensing data showing the Commerce Department approved about 879,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese companies from December 2025 to May 2026, out of 3.4 million requested. Tencent received approval for 150,000, Alibaba 75,000, Baidu 43,000 and BYD 4,000. Nvidia said approvals carried strict conditions and that it has since stopped shipping H200 chips to China. Separately, a 16 November rule requires licences for data centres anywhere that could serve Chinese firms, with existing operators given 90 days.
stories.market: The data feed political pressure for tighter controls just as Nvidia faces state and federal probes; Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil now need licences for advanced chips, a hit to Southeast Asian data-centre builders.

stories.headline: Google Prices Gemini 4 Neon at $3 per Million Tokens as Citi Shifts AI-Agent Liability to Customers
stories.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon with a one-million-token context window, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Citi updated its account terms so customers are liable for actions taken by third-party AI agents they give account access to. Microsoft made its Decision 1.1 product generally available, saying it runs more than twice as fast and has over 4,000 customers.
stories.market: Price competition among model providers is a theme investors will now measure against Anthropic's public valuation; banks setting liability rules for AI agents matter for fintech and payments adoption.

stories.headline: Alibaba sued in New York over alleged hidden ties to Megaspeed in the Nvidia scandal
stories.summary: An Alibaba shareholder filed a proposed class action in Manhattan federal court on Thursday 19 November against the company and CEO Eddie Wu. The complaint says Alibaba played down export-control risks in its 2024, 2025 and 2026 annual reports while it was, according to media reports cited by the plaintiff, the dominant customer of Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the centre of the Nvidia chip-diversion scandal. The class covers buyers of Alibaba's US depositary shares from 23 May 2024 to 11 November 2026. The suit links a 14% four-day fall in the shares last week to reports on those ties and to a 12 November Reuters report on possible tighter US curbs on Chinese firms' remote use of advanced chips. Damages are unspecified, and Alibaba did not immediately comment.
stories.market: Alibaba ADSs (BABA) lost 14% over four sessions last week, per the complaint; the case adds US litigation risk to Chinese AI and cloud names already exposed to export-control headlines.

body: The lead plaintiff, shareholder Withida Bihan, accuses Alibaba and Eddie Wu of knowingly understating export-control risk in three consecutive annual reports. The complaint centres on Alibaba's alleged business with Megaspeed, a Singapore company suspected of helping Beijing obtain advanced Nvidia AI chips.

The plaintiff argues the risk came to light last week, when media reports on Megaspeed's links to Alibaba and to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive linked to ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, coincided with a 14% fall in the ADSs over four days. The suit also points to a Reuters report on 12 November that the scandal could lead Washington to restrict Chinese AI companies' remote access to advanced processors.

The case adds to Alibaba's US legal disputes. In June it sued the US government over its addition to the Pentagon's list of Chinese military companies, and in October a California federal judge granted it an injunction on a related lobbying restriction. On the day the suit was filed, Wu said Alibaba remained on track for $100 billion in external cloud revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin by 2030.

stories.headline: Newsmax sues to unwind Fox's $22 billion Roku takeover
stories.summary: Newsmax filed a federal antitrust suit in California on Wednesday 18 November seeking to halt the integration of Roku into Fox and ultimately force a divestiture or unwind of the $22 billion deal, which closed on 6 November. The complaint, brought under the Clayton Act, alleges Fox's Tubi and The Roku Channel together hold more than 70% of US free, ad-supported streaming TV viewing. It also challenges the Justice Department's decision to close its review on the strength of Fox commitments announced in a press release rather than a court-enforceable consent decree. Fox called the suit wholly without merit and says Roku will remain an open platform.
stories.market: Fox Corp (FOXA) faces integration uncertainty on its largest deal; a private challenge to a closed merger rarely succeeds but can slow integration and synergy plans.

body: Newsmax wants a court to order Roku run independently while the case proceeds, and in the end to make Fox sell Tubi or The Roku Channel or reverse the acquisition. It argues the combination gives Fox outsized control over free streaming TV and the means to disadvantage rival news providers; Newsmax2 is carried on The Roku Channel but not on Tubi.

The Justice Department closed its review after Fox pledged to keep distributing competing content, avoid discriminatory search results and protect third-party viewing data. Newsmax says those pledges are not enforceable because they were set out in a DOJ press release rather than a consent decree, and that Fox rejected its request for a binding agreement on the same terms.
Fox said the deal had passed a rigorous regulatory review and that integration began after closing. Roku's operating system reaches more than 100 million households, according to the complaint.

stories.summary: The US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit declined on 19 November to revive a lawsuit by cardholders, reported as California cardholders, against Visa, Mastercard and major banks over interchange fees. The decision leaves the cardholders' claims dismissed; the panel's full reasoning was not available to us at press time.
stories.market: Removes one consumer-side liability for Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA); merchant swipe-fee litigation and settlements remain the main legal overhang.

stories.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia as the SEC probe widens the legal fallout from Huang's exit
stories.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office served Nvidia with a subpoena on Thursday 19 November, seeking to establish whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether the company misled investors or the public about that risk. It follows a Wall Street Journal report on 17 November that the SEC has opened a civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. What is new since yesterday: the matter has moved from congressional pressure to two formal investigations, one state and one federal. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 12 November; interim CEO Colette Kress and new chairman Harvey Jones are running the company, and the board said on 17 November it does not intend to reinstate him. A subpoena is an investigative step, not a finding of wrongdoing.
stories.market: Nvidia (NVDA) had fallen more than 10% since Huang's departure as of 17 November, per TechCrunch; the probes add disclosure and legal-liability risk to the stock and spill into Chinese AI names such as Alibaba (BABA).

body: Nvidia now faces formal scrutiny on two fronts. On Thursday, California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office issued a subpoena to the chipmaker, two days after Bonta said publicly that his office was looking at the matter. The state wants material that would show whether Nvidia broke California law, focusing on whether advanced processors or confidential information found their way to China and whether investors were told enough about that risk.

At federal level, the Wall Street Journal reported on 17 November, citing people familiar with the matter, that the SEC has opened a civil inquiry into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. The scope has not been made public. Separately, a long-running federal probe into Singapore-based Megaspeed, suspected of helping channel Nvidia AI chips to China, began at the Commerce Department in late 2024 and moved to the Justice Department in 2025, according to Forbes.

The scandal broke on 29 October, when the New York Times reported a close relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive (the two are not related). Nvidia's board opened an inquiry on 8 November into whether Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and Huang resigned as president, CEO and director on 12 November. Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones board chairman; the board has hired a firm to search for a permanent successor.

Huang apologised publicly on 17 November and said he would return if asked. The same day, Jones told the earnings call the board had unanimously accepted the resignation and does not intend to reinstate him, though Semafor reported some directors still favour his return.

Congress is also involved. Three House committees have scheduled a transcribed interview with Huang for 1 December, with Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter due the following day, and Senator Tim Scott said Huang agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next month. Plaintiff firms have also announced securities class-action investigations.

stories.headline: US gives Lukoil asset buyers four more weeks to negotiate
stories.summary: The US Treasury's OFAC issued General License 131L on 19 November, two days before its predecessor expired, allowing talks and contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH to continue until 19 December 2026. Maintenance and wind-down of the international unit's operations is authorised until 20 February 2027. Any sale still needs separate OFAC approval, and no money may flow to persons or accounts in Russia. The portfolio was initially valued at about $22 billion; Carlyle, which agreed a deal in January, dropped its bid in October, and at least a dozen parties including Exxon Mobil have shown interest, Reuters reported on 22 October.
stories.market: The extension keeps a roughly $22 billion refining, trading and retail portfolio in limbo; it matters for European fuel supply chains and for any bidder seeking discounted downstream assets.

body: GL 131L replaces GL 131K, which had been due to lapse on 21 November. It lets parties negotiate and sign contracts, agreements in principle, binding memoranda and bids for Lukoil International GmbH and entities it owns at least 50% of, as long as performance depends on a separate OFAC licence.

A second part of the licence lets the unit keep operating or wind down existing contracts until 20 February 2027, and allows its blocked accounts to be used for those transactions. Unblocking property and transfers to Russia remain banned. OFAC also updated two related FAQs.

Washington sanctioned Lukoil and Rosneft in October 2025. Carlyle agreed in January 2026 to buy the international assets excluding Kazakhstan but withdrew in October, leaving the field open to other bidders.

stories.headline: SEC sues eight Colorado entities over $37 million fake-crypto-platform fraud
stories.summary: The SEC on 19 November charged eight Colorado-registered entities in federal court in Colorado, alleging they took more than $37 million from over 1,500 US investors between about August 2024 and May 2026. The agency says the firms operated in four pairs of a purported investment adviser and a sham crypto trading platform, each lasting about six months, and were likely run from overseas. Victims were reached through social-media ads and group chats. The SEC seeks injunctions, disgorgement with interest, civil penalties and industry bars.
stories.market: No listed issuer is involved; the case signals continued SEC focus on retail crypto fraud even as overall enforcement has fallen.

body: The defendants are four adviser-and-platform pairs: WeChat Capital with Tech Brokerage Asset Alliance, HB Wealth Advisors with IdeaCrypto Exchange, Convergent Wealth Advisors with RealSimple Crypto Exchange, and Associated Wealth Advisors with Essential Crypto Exchange. All eight face anti-fraud charges under Rule 10b-5, and the four advisers also face Advisers Act charges.

The SEC also took down a Form D and two Forms ADV linked to the scheme from its website. The case comes after the agency reported 348 enforcement actions and $1.095 billion in monetary relief for the fiscal year to 30 September 2026.

stories.headline: Brussels presses seven states to scrap tax rules that penalise foreign pension funds
stories.summary: The European Commission's November infringement package, published 19 November, opened cases against Germany, Spain, Italy, Austria, Poland, Portugal and Romania over tax rules it says discriminate against foreign pension funds and life insurers, and widened an existing case against Belgium. It also challenged Luxembourg's tax exemption on interest from its Defence Bond as a barrier to cross-border investment in government debt. On markets rules, Spain, France and Romania received reasoned opinions for failing to transpose MiFID II changes on consolidated-tape sanctions, due by 29 September 2025, and Spain and Portugal were pursued over MiCA-related banking rules.
stories.market: If the tax cases succeed, cross-border pension funds and insurers could recover withholding taxes on European equity and bond income; the Luxembourg case touches retail sovereign-bond products.

stories.headline: Street Dollars Climb: Argentina's Blue Sets a Record at ARS 1,640 as the Naira Hits ₦1,470
stories.summary: Argentina's informal "blue" dollar closed at ARS 1,640 on 19 Nov, up ARS 10 on the day and a record high, according to El Litoral and El Cronista, about 3.5% above the ARS 1,585 official Banco Nación rate. El Cronista put the CCL rate at ARS 1,725.90 around midday and central-bank reserves at $49.55 billion. In Lagos, the naira weakened to ₦1,470 per dollar on the street on 19 Nov, its weakest since 28 Jan, against ₦1,363.23 in the official market on 18 Nov. Iran's open-market rate was steady at 2,714,000 rials per dollar on 20 Nov after a 1.65% rise the day before. New since yesterday: both the peso and the naira lost further ground on the street.
stories.market: Wider gaps between street and official rates signal pressure on Argentina's crawling band and on Nigeria's reserves ahead of December demand for dollars; El Cronista links the peso pressure to year-end bonus payments.

body: In Argentina, the blue dollar has gained ARS 65 in November after ending October at ARS 1,565, El Cronista reported. The MEP rate closed at ARS 1,636.18. The wholesale rate remains well below the ARS 1,974.20 ceiling of the official band, which is now adjusted monthly for inflation.

In Nigeria, the street rate has fallen from ₦1,390 on 13 Nov to ₦1,470, a gap of roughly ₦107 to the official window. stories.headline: US Sanctions the Comancheros Biker Gang and a Toronto 'Ndrangheta Faction
stories.summary: OFAC on 19 Nov designated the Australia-based Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang and leaders of a Toronto-area faction of Italy's 'Ndrangheta under its illicit-drugs sanctions programme. Fourteen individuals were listed, including the gang's Spain-based world commander and Australia-based world president, along with four Ontario businesses: three funeral-home companies and a limousine firm linked to Luigi Vescio Sr. Treasury said the Comancheros have helped move multi-hundred-kilogram cocaine shipments from South America and work with Latin American cartels, while the 'Ndrangheta operates in more than 80 countries. The action was coordinated with police in Australia, New Zealand, Italy and Canada.
stories.market: Banks in Canada, Australia and the US must block any assets of the listed people and firms; Treasury says the Toronto faction launders proceeds through US and Canadian financial systems, putting correspondent-banking compliance in focus.

body: The Comancheros designations cover leaders in Spain, Australia and New Zealand and a supplier of encrypted phones to the group. Treasury linked the gang to the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, Clan del Golfo and Ecuador's Los Choneros.

On the 'Ndrangheta side, Treasury listed six alleged leaders of the Toronto faction plus three Vescio family members and four Ontario companies. The 'Ndrangheta itself was first sanctioned in 2008 under the Kingpin Act; its OFAC entry has been updated.

OFAC issued a general licence allowing a wind-down of transactions with the newly blocked parties. Separately on the same day it amended a Russia-related general licence (131L) covering negotiations over a sale of Lukoil International GmbH.

stories.headline: Spain's Balearics Flagged as a Shadow-Fleet Corridor as EU Boardings and Ukrainian Sanctions Mount
stories.summary: A report published on 19 Nov by the Majorca Daily Bulletin, drawing on Spanish strategic-studies research, says more than 80 suspect shadow-fleet vessels move through the Mediterranean each month, with the Balearic Islands a key transit lane. The EU's Operation Irini, whose mandate was widened this year, boarded the Aframax tanker Midag on 13 Nov and the bloc's foreign-policy chief said the inspection confirmed it was sailing under a false Zimbabwean flag; the ship was not seized. Ukraine on 17 Nov sanctioned seven more Russian-flagged ships it says carry military cargo, after listing 39 oil-carrying vessels in late October. Across the US, UK and EU, 1,225 tankers were under sanctions at end-September, according to S&P Global data.
stories.market: Tighter policing of the Mediterranean route adds to the cost of moving Russian crude and keeps tanker freight high; Washington is weighing case-by-case approvals for clean buyers to take 50-80 sanctioned tankers back into lawful trade to ease rates.

stories.headline: FBI Ties North Korea to $400 Million in Deepfake-Call Crypto Thefts as the Binance Hacker Moves Another $248 Million
stories.summary: The US Justice Department and FBI on 19 Nov unveiled an operation they call "FaceStealer", saying North Korean hackers stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over about 18 months by luring targets into fake video calls. Investigators seized cloud infrastructure used in the campaign and, under a federal warrant, took possession of more than 900 webcam recordings of victims. The same day, on-chain tracker Lookonchain reported that the wallets behind the 29 Oct Binance theft moved another 137,602 ETH, worth about $248 million, after 75,000 ETH (about $136 million) left two theft-linked wallets on 17 Nov. The Associated Press puts the Binance loss at about $6.3 billion, the largest crypto heist on record; more than $2.7 billion has been frozen and a court has authorised the seizure or restriction of over $1.2 billion.
stories.market: The Binance loot is being rotated into bitcoin, XRP, TRX and SOL via cross-chain bridges and swaps, keeping exchanges and stablecoin issuers on alert for freezes; Binance says it has replaced 98% of affected customer tokens from its own funds. No clear price effect on ETH or BNB was reported in today's sources.

sources.name: The Cool Down (citing DOJ, FBI, AP, DW)

body: The FBI says FaceStealer is run by North Korean hackers separate from TraderTraitor, the military-linked unit it blames for the Binance breach. German broadcaster DW links FaceStealer to the group known as Sapphire Sleet, or UNC1069. Most victims worked in crypto or other internet businesses, and the Justice Department warned that attacks on open-source developers could spread the damage well beyond the individual targets.

Enforcement steps announced on 19 Nov include the seizure of cloud infrastructure and the FBI taking custody of more than 900 webcam videos recorded from victims. Recovered funds will go through civil forfeiture, where judges decide who is entitled to them. A senior Justice Department national-security official said Pyongyang uses crypto theft to fund its weapons programmes.

The Binance case continues to dominate the laundering picture. According to Elliptic data cited by crypto.news, stolen funds have been spread across nearly 27,000 wallets on at least 16 blockchains, with roughly 3,900 BTC (about $250 million) gathered in fresh addresses. At least 11,000 ETH has gone through the Tornado Cash mixer since 8 Nov and about 700 BTC through CoinJoin since 1 Nov.

Elliptic estimated that about $2.56 billion still sat in theft-linked addresses as of 17 Nov and that only a negligible amount had likely been cashed out, though some may have reached Chinese laundering networks. Binance's own review found about $2.85 billion frozen or intercepted.

stories.headline: Treasury Sanctions a Cambodian Scam-Compound Owner and Two Myanmar Militia Commanders
stories.summary: The US Treasury's OFAC on 19 Nov sanctioned three people and two companies tied to Southeast Asian online-scam centres. The targets are Cambodian national Zhao Hui, described as a scam-compound owner who paid protection money to Prince Group chief Chen Zhi, plus two Phnom Penh firms he chairs, and two commanders of Myanmar's Democratic Karen Benevolent Army, including its commander-in-chief. It is the third round of scam-centre designations in about ten weeks, after a 9 Sep action on Xinbi Guarantee and a 5 Nov package against the Prince Group network. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report logged $7.2 billion of reported crypto-investment-fraud losses from more than 61,000 complaints.
stories.market: Sanctions freeze any US-linked assets and bar dealings with the listed parties, raising compliance pressure on exchanges, stablecoin issuers and payment firms that process flows from Cambodia and the Thai-Myanmar border.

stories.headline: Private-Credit Defaults Nearly Double in the Third Quarter, Houlihan Lokey Finds
stories.summary: The size-weighted default rate in US direct lending rose to 1.5% of outstanding principal in the third quarter of 2026 from 0.8% in the second, according to Houlihan Lokey data released on 19 Nov. By count, defaults climbed to 3.7% from 2.5%. Smaller borrowers with under $100 million of EBITDA were hit hardest, with a 5.0% count-based rate, and 11% of lower-middle-market loans are now marked below 90 cents on the dollar, against roughly 1% in 2023. Healthcare led sector defaults at 7.1% by count, while software stayed among the lowest at 1.0% size-weighted.
stories.market: Rising defaults and markdowns weigh on business development companies and other listed lenders with heavy exposure to small and healthcare borrowers, and feed the debate over banks' links to the sector.

stories.headline: ECB Puts Banks' Private-Credit Ties Under the Microscope as US Nominees Play Down the Risk
stories.summary: The European Central Bank on 19 Nov made banks' links to private-credit funds and other non-bank lenders a supervisory priority for 2027-29, announcing a new round of on-site inspections covering fund financing, asset-based lending and exposures to private-equity and private-credit funds. The ECB said earlier exercises found most participating banks lacked stress tests or risk limits designed for non-banks, though supervisory board chair Claudia Buch said direct exposures remain relatively small. The same day in Washington, nominees for the SEC and a senior Treasury post told the Senate Banking Committee that concerns over banks' private-credit exposure were overstated, according to American Banker.
stories.market: Closer ECB scrutiny could raise capital and risk-management costs for euro-area banks active in fund finance and prime brokerage, a growing fee business for the region's largest lenders.

body: The ECB said banks' dealings with non-bank financial institutions grew over the past year and are concentrated in a small number of institutions. It also noted a surge in redemption requests at semi-liquid private-credit vehicles earlier in 2026, without broad deterioration.

Supervisors will follow up on earlier recommendations on financing private-equity and credit funds and will focus on banks with large exposures to riskier counterparties. AI-related financing risks will also be monitored.
In Washington, Senate Republicans are moving to confirm the regulatory nominees before control of Congress changes in January.

stories.headline: Anthropic Opens at $111.50, Closes Up 17% as a Falling Market Trims the Pop
stories.summary: Anthropic's ANT shares first traded at $111.50 just after 11:30 a.m. ET on Thursday 19 Nov, 34% above the $83 IPO price, touched $115.10 and then faded to close at $97.17, up 17.07%. The record $81.3bn offering of 980 million shares had been priced above an original $70-$78 range. The opening cross alone moved about 108 million shares, and roughly 139 million (about $15bn) changed hands in the first full minute. In after-hours trade the stock slipped to $92.60, 4.7% below the close (as of 19:59 ET). Several brokers and research houses initiated coverage with targets between $105 and $155, while Morningstar put fair value at $92.
stories.market: The debut landed on a down day: the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.3% to 23,879.20 and Nvidia lost 3.3%, and Asia extended the AI selloff on Friday with the Nikkei and Kospi both down about 4.5% in morning trade. ANT's fade from its open is being read as a gauge of appetite for frontier-AI equity supply.

body: Anthropic's first day on Nasdaq delivered a solid gain but not the blow-out some pre-market indicators implied. Bloomberg-cited indications had pointed to an open near $103.40, and perpetual futures on Hyperliquid traded around $105.50 at 10:30 a.m. ET (per Forbes). The actual first print came in higher, at $111.50, shortly after 11:30 a.m. ET.

From the intraday high of $115.10 the stock gave back much of its premium as the broader market slid, finishing at $97.17, a gain of $14.17 or 17.07% on the $83 offer price. After the bell it eased further to $92.60 (as of 19:59 ET on 19 Nov).

The deal raised $81.3bn from 980 million Class A shares, topping SpaceX's $75bn listing in June as the largest IPO on record. Terms were lifted during marketing from 825 million shares at $70-$78. The retail allocation was cut to 15% from a targeted 20%, and Stocktwits reported that a separate $26bn private placement brings expected net proceeds to about $104.8bn.

Valuation figures vary by share count: Yahoo Finance's headline put the closing valuation near $1.27 trillion, while fully diluted measures run higher. The lock-up is staggered across 23 expiry dates, running out to the second full trading day after results for the quarter ending 30 Sept 2027, with tranches from 174 million to 3 billion shares.
Vanda Research said retail traders were active on both sides of the trade rather than buying in one direction. A Stocktwits poll of about 17,500 users found 68% planned to avoid the stock for now.
detail.consensus: Initiating targets reported on 19 Nov span $92 (Morningstar fair value) to $155 (Melius), with most clustered between $125 and $150.

stories.headline: Intuit Sells Mailchimp for $3.68 Billion, Under a Third of What It Paid
stories.summary: Intuit agreed on 19 Nov to sell Mailchimp to Italy's Bending Spoons for about $3.68bn: $3.31bn in cash and $368m in new Bending Spoons shares. Intuit paid $12bn for the email-marketing business in 2021. Fiscal Q1 revenue rose 12% to $4.35bn and adjusted EPS jumped 56% to $2.91, while Mailchimp revenue slipped 1% to $313m. Intuit trimmed its full-year revenue outlook to $23.08bn-$23.37bn, cut Credit Karma growth to 3%-7% from 11%-13% and kept adjusted EPS guidance at $22.88-$23.12. The shares were down 14.6% at 16:15 ET after the release and 9.5% lower at 18:01 ET.
stories.market: INTU's after-hours drop drags on mid-cap fintech and consumer-finance software sentiment; Bending Spoons, listed on Nasdaq since July, adds another large purchase after agreeing to buy Airtable and Miro. Intuit plans to use the proceeds for buybacks before the end of fiscal 2027.

body: Intuit is unwinding the largest acquisition in its history. The $3.68bn price tag for Mailchimp, including its legal entity The Rocket Science Group, is less than a third of the $12bn Intuit agreed to pay in 2021. Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

Bending Spoons will pay $3.31bn in cash, and Intuit will take $368m in newly issued Bending Spoons stock. The Milan-based buyer, whose portfolio already includes Evernote, Vimeo, WeTransfer, Eventbrite and AOL, has also agreed deals for Airtable ($1.285bn) and Miro ($1.355bn) since its July listing.

The quarter itself was strong: revenue up 12% to $4.35bn and adjusted operating income up 46% to $1.05bn. The pressure came from the outlook, with Credit Karma's growth forecast cut sharply to 3%-7%. Q2 guidance calls for revenue of $4.93bn-$4.95bn and adjusted EPS of $3.17-$3.22.
The stock fell 14.55% at 16:15 ET before paring the move to a 9.52% decline by 18:01 ET.

stories.headline: BASF Walks Away From Evonik; Evonik Shares Sink 17.6%
stories.summary: New today: a day after reports that BASF was offering job and site guarantees to revive its approach, the company said on 19 Nov that it had ended its pursuit of Evonik after two non-binding all-cash proposals were rejected. Its final offer was €24 a share, about €11.2bn, up from an initial €22.15 (about €10.3bn) in September. BASF said it would have considered only a modest further increase and that paying more would not serve its shareholders. Evonik closed 17.6% lower, and BASF rose 0.6% (Newsquawk wrap, 19 Nov).
stories.market: Evonik's fall erased the bid premium and helped make chemicals the weakest Stoxx 600 sector on 19 Nov; BASF shares edged up as investors welcomed capital discipline.

body: BASF said Evonik's executive board had not engaged meaningfully until the day of the announcement, and that its view of Evonik's standalone prospects did not justify paying more than a further modest increase over €24.

Evonik had rejected both offers as too low and argued it has a viable independent plan, citing job protection until 2032 and about €5bn of planned investment. BASF had written to the RAG Foundation, Evonik's largest shareholder, offering possible commitments on plants, jobs and training.

BASF chairman Markus Kamieth framed the decision as part of the Winning Ways strategy, under which acquisitions are optional rather than essential, and reaffirmed a focus on shareholder distributions.
Evonik shares were down 17% at 14:20 GMT and closed 17.6% lower; BASF was up 1.2% intraday and closed 0.6% higher.

stories.headline: Boston Scientific Sells $3 Billion and €4.25 Billion of Bonds for Penumbra; Weaker Issuers Pull Back
stories.summary: Boston Scientific priced $3.0bn of dollar notes and €4.25bn of euro notes on 19 Nov to help pay for its acquisition of Penumbra. Dollar coupons run from 5.375% (2029) to 5.875% (2036), and euro coupons from 3.875% (2028) to 5.125% (2046), plus a €500m floater. At the other end of the market, Everforth withdrew a planned $500m senior notes sale, citing market conditions, and fell 10.1%. SELLAS Life Sciences sold 11.5m shares at $13 to raise $150m, about 28% below its prior close, and dropped 17.2%. Vivid Seats jumped 63.3% on a recapitalization with most term-loan lenders that it says will cut net debt by about $232m.
stories.market: Investment-grade acquirers can still fund deals at sub-6% dollar coupons, but a 2% equity selloff on 19 Nov shut the door on at least one high-yield deal. Discounted follow-ons continue to be punished.

body: Boston Scientific's dollar deal has four tranches: $1.0bn of 5.375% 2029s, $750m of 5.5% 2031s, $750m of 5.75% 2033s and $500m of 5.875% 2036s. The euro deal, issued through American Medical Systems Europe B.V., has six tranches, from a €500m 2028 floater to €750m of 5.125% 2046s.
Both offerings are due to settle on 1 Dec. If the Penumbra acquisition does not close in time, the fixed-rate notes must be redeemed at 101%.

In riskier corners, Everforth's withdrawn $500m deal and SELLAS's discounted $150m share sale show that issuers are paying for volatility, while Vivid Seats rallied after reaching agreement with lenders.

stories.headline: Walmart Raises Its Outlook Again as Ads Jump 25%, but Shares Slip 1%
stories.summary: Walmart reported fiscal Q3 revenue up 5.2% to $188.8bn (4.5% in constant currency) and adjusted EPS of $0.65 on 19 Nov. US comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, slower than 4.5% a year earlier. Global e-commerce rose 17%, and advertising grew 25%, with US advertising up 37%. Walmart lifted its full-year constant-currency sales growth forecast to 4.9%-5.2% from 4.0%-5.0% and adjusted EPS to $2.84-$2.89 from $2.80-$2.87. The stock closed 1.04% lower in a market that fell about 2%.
stories.market: WMT outperformed the S&P 500's 2.0% drop, but the slower US comp held back the reaction. A shift in Flipkart's Big Billion Days moved about 5 points of international sales growth from Q3 into Q4.

stories.headline: Ross Falls 7% After Hours on a Tariff-Flattered Guide; Gap Rises Despite a Cut
stories.summary: Ross Stores reported Q3 EPS of $1.91, up from $1.58, on sales up 12% to $6.26bn and comparable sales up 8%. It raised full-year EPS guidance to $8.75-$8.84 from $8.61-$8.77, but the new range includes about $0.60 from tariff refunds. The stock, already down 3.4% at the close at $219.88, fell about 7% after hours. Gap's Q3 sales rose 2% to $4.0bn with flat comps: the Gap brand grew 9%, Athleta fell 15% and Banana Republic fell 3%. Gap cut its adjusted EPS guidance to $2.29-$2.34 from $2.35-$2.45, yet the stock rose 3.6% after hours at 18:02 ET.
stories.market: Off-price retail sold off after hours (ROST), while the apparel reaction was mixed; investors appear to be discounting one-off IEEPA tariff refunds that are lifting several retailers' reported earnings.

body: Ross's Q4 guidance calls for comparable sales up 4%-5% and EPS of $2.16-$2.25. Because the raised full-year range is smaller than the roughly $0.60 tariff-refund benefit included in it, the underlying outlook implies little or no improvement. Operating margin was 12.3%, above the company's 11.7%-12.0% plan.

Gap reported diluted EPS of $0.86, or $0.82 excluding an IEEPA tariff recovery. It now expects full-year sales to be roughly flat, against earlier guidance of 1%-1.5% growth, and adjusted operating margin of about 7.2%, down from 7.4%-7.6%. The company said the fourth quarter had started more slowly than expected.

stories.headline: Williams-Sonoma Drops 15% as StoneX and Liquidity Services Slump
stories.summary: Williams-Sonoma closed 15.16% lower on 19 Nov after adjusted EPS of $2.19 missed estimates by $0.02. Revenue rose 5.8% to $1.99bn, just below expectations, and the company only reiterated its full-year outlook. StoneX fell 26.7% even though Q4 net operating revenue rose 12% to $655.2m, as net income slipped 2% to $84.2m. Liquidity Services lost 24.9% on a 10% revenue decline to $106.4m. Valvoline rose 10.4% on 22% sales growth to $554m, while UGI fell 7.75% after announcing plans to spin off its global LPG arm and guiding fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS to $2.90-$3.20.
stories.market: Richly valued names were punished for small misses: WSM traded at 26 times forward earnings before the drop, against a five-year average of 16 times.

stories.headline: PDD Jumps 11% on Profit Growth While NetEase Sinks 11%
stories.summary: Temu owner PDD Holdings rose 11.04% on 19 Nov after operating profit climbed to RMB31.2bn from RMB25.0bn on flat revenue of RMB108.3bn. Non-GAAP net income was RMB31.0bn, little changed from RMB31.4bn. NetEase fell 11.39% as Q3 net revenue slipped 1.8% to RMB27.9bn. Alibaba lost 1.26% after reporting a September-quarter free cash outflow of RMB34.5bn tied to cloud spending, even as AI cloud revenue grew 53%.
stories.market: US-listed Chinese stocks diverged on results, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell almost 2% to 22,393.93 in Friday morning trade (20 Nov) as the regional AI selloff spread.

stories.headline: Soitec Surges 18% and Babcock Gains, While JD Sports Narrows Its Profit Range
stories.summary: French chip-materials maker Soitec jumped 18% on 19 Nov after first-half revenue and EBITDA beat forecasts. It now expects revenue to rise about 40% in fiscal 2027. UK defence group Babcock gained 6.5% after first-half revenue and profit beat estimates and it reaffirmed its FY27 outlook. JD Sports Fashion fell 4.2% as Q3 like-for-like sales dropped 1.8% and it narrowed FY27 pretax profit guidance to £700m-£750m from £700m-£800m. Those moves came as the Stoxx 600 traded about 0.2% lower mid-afternoon (per Newsquawk, 15:20 UTC).
stories.market: Soitec's outlook offered a rare positive read for European semiconductor suppliers on a day of global tech selling; JD's narrower range weighed on UK sportswear retail.

stories.headline: Nvidia Targets Keep Falling: Freedom Broker Cuts to $230 as Volume Doubles
stories.summary: Freedom Broker cut its Nvidia price target to $230 from $305 on 19 Nov while keeping a Buy rating, a day after Wells Fargo lowered its target to $250 from $300 (Overweight). On 18 Nov, BMO reiterated Outperform with a $240 target and DA Davidson reiterated Buy at $200. Nvidia reversed an early 4.7% gain to close down 3.3% at about $145.98, from a prior close of $150.96. About 312.7m shares traded, 96% above the daily average. The average target among covering analysts is $263.66, and the stock now trades well below its 50-day ($210.30) and 200-day ($203.56) moving averages.
stories.market: NVDA's reversal on Anthropic's debut day dragged the Nasdaq down 2.3% and fed Friday's 4.5% drops in the Nikkei and Kospi, where Advantest, SoftBank Group and Samsung Electronics led losses.

body: Brokers are reducing Nvidia targets after Jensen Huang's sudden resignation as chief executive earlier this month, though most are keeping positive ratings. MarketBeat's tally shows 3 Strong Buy, 43 Buy and 15 Hold ratings, giving an average rating of Moderate Buy.
Thursday's 312.7m-share session was close to double normal volume. Nvidia's market value stood at about $3.52 trillion as of the 19 Nov close.
Earlier downgrades include Craig-Hallum's cut to Hold with a $180 target on 12 Nov.
detail.consensus: MarketBeat consensus is Moderate Buy with an average target of $263.66 (as of 19 Nov).

stories.headline: Positioning: Hedge Funds' Tech Bets at a Decade Low as Retail Trades Both Sides of ANT
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs prime-brokerage data published on 17 Nov showed hedge funds selling US stocks for a second week through 12 Nov. Their long-to-short ratio in tech fell to 1.5, the lowest since 2016, from a June peak of 2.14. Thursday's tape fit that defensive stance: the S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,175.83 for a sixth straight loss, and the Dow fell 1,101 points to 49,097.06. Nvidia volume ran 96% above average. In Anthropic's debut, about 139m shares (about $15bn) traded in the first full minute, and Vanda Research said retail accounts were both buying and selling rather than piling in one way.
stories.market: Light tech net exposure leaves room for short-covering rallies, which Goldman has flagged as a squeeze risk, but long-only selling of Nvidia continues; consumer discretionary saw the strongest hedge-fund buying in more than three months.

body: Goldman's prime-services team said the week to 12 Nov was the fifth week of net selling in six. The selling came mainly from new single-stock shorts, partly offset by short covering and purchases of macro products, and the bank called it a rotation rather than a broad retreat.

Funds sold 8 of 11 sectors, led by technology, financials, health care and consumer staples. Financials selling was the heaviest in eight months, while consumer discretionary saw the largest net buying in more than three months.
The 19 Nov session showed that pressure: Nvidia traded 312.7m shares, and the US indexes posted their sixth straight decline.

stories.headline: Philly Fed Slumps to 6.3 While Prices Paid Jump, Feeding Hike Fears
stories.summary: The Philadelphia Fed's factory index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9, far below the 20.0 expected, while its prices-paid gauge leapt to 58.2 from 43.2 (data released 19 Nov). Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 against 197,000 forecast, and continuing claims climbed 70,000 to 1.763 million. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said inflation remains well above the 2% target.
stories.market: The mix of slowing activity and hotter input prices kept a December Fed hike priced in, yet Treasuries rallied on safe-haven demand: the 10-year yield ended at 5.048% and the 2-year at 4.766% (19 Nov close).

body: Thursday's data painted a stagflation-tinged picture. Manufacturing activity in the Philadelphia region slowed sharply, with the headline index dropping to 6.3 from 20.9, but firms reported a big jump in what they pay for inputs, with the prices-paid index rising to 58.2 from 43.2.

Initial claims for the week to 14 Nov were 203,000, above the roughly 197,000 consensus, and the prior week was revised up to 202,000. The four-week average rose to 197,750. Continuing claims for the week to 7 Nov rose 70,000 to 1.763 million, the clearest sign that laid-off workers are taking longer to find jobs.

Fed officials stayed hawkish. Goolsbee said inflation is well above target while describing the labour market as stable, and Governor Waller has raised the option of a half-point move in December. As of 18 Nov, futures implied roughly a 96% chance of a quarter-point December hike from the current 3.75%-4.00% range.

Bonds moved the other way to the data on the day: the 10-year yield slipped back to 5.048% and the 2-year to 4.766% as investors sought safety, while the dollar firmed broadly and USD/JPY reached 159.68.

stories.headline: Loonie Slips Below 70 US Cents as the Rate Gap With the Fed Widens
stories.summary: The Canadian dollar traded around 69.88 US cents on 19 Nov after several weeks of losses, its weakest level against the greenback since March 2025, according to BMO. Strategists blame the gap between the Bank of Canada's 2.50% policy rate and the Fed's 3.75%-4.00% range, with US rates heading higher faster than Canadian ones.
stories.market: A sub-70-cent loonie lifts Canadian exporters' US-dollar earnings but raises import costs; Scotiabank's Shaun Osborne says Canadian short-term rates have risen, just not as far as US rates.

stories.headline: Real Hits a 19-Month Low Despite a $1 Billion Central-Bank Sale
stories.summary: Brazil's central bank sold US$1 billion of reserves outright on 19 Nov, but the dollar still closed near R$5.93, up about 1.1% for a sixth straight gain and the real's weakest close in 19 months. Debt worries and hawkish Fed minutes outweighed the Senate's 18 Nov approval of a spending-curb bill, which now heads to the lower house.
stories.market: The dollar has risen 5.4% against the real since 10 Nov, cutting the dollar value of Brazilian stocks and bonds; the Ibovespa fell about 0.7% on 19 Nov, and local markets are shut on 20 Nov for a holiday.

body: The central bank's spot sale of US$1 billion, executed at R$5.86 per dollar, briefly pulled the dollar lower on Thursday morning, but it was back above R$5.90 within hours and closed near R$5.93.
The sale amounted to about 0.3% of reserves, which stood at US$365 billion at the end of October, enough to slow the move but not to change how traders view Brazil's debt trajectory.

The Senate passed Complementary Bill 299/2026 on 18 Nov, which the government says could improve the 2027 budget by up to R$56.1 billion. The lower house may vote on it in an extraordinary session on Monday, 23 Nov.

External pressure added to the slide: October Fed minutes pointed to further US hikes, pulling money from emerging markets. Prediction-market traders put the odds of no change at the central bank's December meeting at about 78%.

Fear of a December Fed hike drove the selling, while Banxico's cut to 6.25% on 5 Nov has narrowed the yield gap that draws foreign money.

stories.headline: Pound Sinks to 1.308, a One-Year Low, as Gilt Yields Hold Above 5.3%
stories.summary: Sterling fell about 0.5% to roughly $1.308 on 19 Nov, holding at a one-year low as the dollar climbed on Fed-hike bets. The 10-year gilt yield ended near 5.32%, up 0.73 points on the year. After October inflation came in slightly below the Bank of England's forecast, traders trimmed the odds of a December hike to about 80% from 90%.
stories.market: A weaker pound adds to imported inflation risk; the BoE raised Bank Rate to 4.00% in November, its first increase since 2023, and markets still price about three more hikes by June (as of 19 Nov).

stories.headline: Sánchez and Feijóo Clash in TV Debate Nine Days Before Spain Votes
stories.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo met in a televised debate on the night of 19 November, ahead of the 29 November general election. A 40dB poll for El País and SER published the same evening put the PP at 32.2% and 134 seats, PSOE at 30.2% and 120, and Vox at 17.6% and 58, giving PP and Vox a combined 192 of 350 seats.
stories.market: A likely change of government is the main domestic risk for Spanish bonds and the IBEX 35, which closed at 19,368 (-0.03%) on 19 November; banks and utilities are the sectors most exposed to tax-policy shifts.

body: Pedro Sánchez and Alberto Núñez Feijóo faced off in a televised debate at 22:00 Madrid time on Thursday 19 November, ten days before the 29 November general election for the 350-seat Congress, where 176 seats make a majority.

A 40dB tracking poll for El País and SER, published hours before the debate, estimated the PP (with UPN) at 32.2% and 134 seats, PSOE at 30.2% and 120 seats and Vox at 17.6% and 58 seats. On those numbers the PP and Vox together would hold 192 seats.

Spanish equities were calm going into the debate: the IBEX 35 closed at 19,368 on 19 November, down 0.03%. A four-way debate is planned for 26 November, although the two main parties have disputed which broadcaster should host it.

stories.summary: The zloty traded at about 4.415 per euro and near 4.01 per dollar on 19 November, after failing to break past 4.03 per dollar a day earlier. Traders cite a relatively dovish National Bank of Poland compared with peers, after October inflation slowed to 3.5%.
stories.market: A softer zloty helps Polish exporters but caps foreign returns on Polish bonds; EUR/PLN has held above 4.40 since the end of October.

body: The zloty hovered around 4.415 per euro after 1 p.m. Warsaw time on 19 November, and USD/PLN drifted back toward 4.01 after failing to clear 4.03 a day earlier, as the dollar index slipped to about 103.6 from 103.9.

Traders attribute the zloty's weakness to uncertainty over domestic policy and a National Bank of Poland outlook seen as relatively dovish next to other central banks. October's flash inflation reading slowed to 3.5% from 4.1%, below a 3.7% forecast, which pushed EUR/PLN above 4.41 at the start of November.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government filed an amendment to the 2027 budget on 19 November to extend the fast-track permitting model of the southern Unified Special Economic Zone to central and northern regions. The government credits the zone with an economic impact of about €60bn in recent years.
stories.market: Faster permits are a modest positive for Italian construction, infrastructure and industrial names; the FTSE MIB rose 0.66% to 50,506 on 19 November, outperforming most of Europe.

stories.headline: Pharma Lifts Swiss Exports 6.3% as Shipments to the US Jump 18%
stories.summary: Swiss exports rose 6.3% month on month to CHF24.7bn in October, data released on 19 November showed, driven by a 15.6% jump in chemicals and pharmaceuticals, while imports fell 2.2% and the trade surplus more than doubled to CHF3.2bn. Exports to the US climbed 18.2%.
stories.market: Stronger pharma shipments support Roche and Novartis earnings expectations; the franc barely reacted, with USD/CHF near 0.8443 on 19 November, close to an 18-month high, as the SNB's 0% rate contrasts with a hawkish Fed.

stories.headline: Brussels Proposes a Fresh €45 Billion Loan to Fill Ukraine's 2027 Gap
stories.summary: The European Commission on 18 November proposed a new €45bn (about $50bn) loan for Ukraine, meant to cover roughly two-thirds of a stated €70bn financing gap for 2027. It splits into €25bn for defence, €10bn for the budget and €10bn of macro-financial aid, and, like the €90bn loan agreed in December 2025, rests on EU budget headroom rather than frozen Russian assets.
stories.market: Secured funding supports Ukraine's reserves and hryvnia stability and eases restructured-Eurobond risk; Euroclear stays out of the plan after Belgium blocked a reparations loan. EU leaders take up the budget at a 26-27 November summit.

body: The European Commission put forward a new €45bn loan for Ukraine on 18 November, aimed at about two-thirds of the €70bn ($77bn) shortfall Kyiv has flagged for 2027. Brussels hopes Canada, Japan, Norway and the UK will fund the remainder.

Of the total, €25bn would go to the defence sector, €10bn to the state budget and €10bn to macro-financial assistance intended to stabilise foreign-currency reserves. The Commission says repayment would come from reparations owed by Russia.

The structure copies the €90bn loan agreed in December 2025, which is backed by headroom in the EU budget. A reparations loan using frozen Russian assets held at Euroclear was blocked by Belgium. The Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary opted out of interest costs on the earlier loan, and Bulgaria has signalled it will join them this time.

The proposal is entangled in talks on the EU's €1.8 trillion 2028-2034 budget: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to halt those talks unless all members contribute to Ukraine. Leaders meet on 26-27 November, aiming for a final deal on 17-18 December.

stories.headline: Rouble Holds Near 82 per Dollar With the Key Rate at 14%
stories.summary: The Bank of Russia set the official dollar rate at 82.2281 roubles for 19 November, up 22 kopecks, while the euro rate fell 45 kopecks to 90.36. Market USD/RUB eased 0.28% to about 82.17 on 19 November, with the central bank's key rate at 14% and inflation near 6.8% against a 4% target.
stories.market: A stable rouble keeps pressure on the budget's rouble-denominated oil revenue but limits imported inflation; the CBR's guidance for an average key rate of 12.5-13.5% in 2027 shapes OFZ yields.

body: The Bank of Russia set its official rates on 18 November for 19 November: 82.2281 roubles per dollar (up 22.48 kopecks), 90.3605 per euro (down 45.31 kopecks) and 12.3004 per yuan (down 4.15 kopecks).

In market trading, USD/RUB eased 0.28% to about 82.17 on 19 November. The rouble had touched about 81 per dollar in late October, its strongest in almost three months, after the central bank held its key rate at 14%.

The central bank expects inflation of 7.1-7.6% by the end of 2026 against a 4% target, with fuel shortages after Ukrainian refinery strikes and wage growth outpacing productivity among the pressures. Its guidance points to an average key rate of 12.5-13.5% in 2027.

stories.headline: Missile Strike Damages PIF's Riyadh Headquarters; Saudi Stocks Dip 0.4%
stories.summary: A suspected Houthi missile damaged the Public Investment Fund's tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District before dawn on 19 Nov; the Saudi-led coalition said falling debris caused material damage. It was the second hit on the financial district in under two weeks, after the Aramco tower was struck on 8 Nov.
stories.market: The Saudi index slipped 0.4% to 10,159 on 19 Nov, led by a 1.5% drop in Saudi National Bank, while Aramco edged up 0.2%; higher US rates also weigh on dollar-pegged Gulf borrowing costs.

body: The coalition said it dealt with a missile threat toward Riyadh early on Thursday and that its initial assessment pointed to debris damage at the PIF tower; it did not say whether the missile was intercepted. Al-Monitor reported damage to several floors and neighbouring buildings and said Saudi authorities reported no casualties.

The coalition also said it intercepted a cruise missile and four ballistic missiles aimed at the south of the kingdom and destroyed a launch platform in Yemen's Saada province. A Houthi spokesman claimed strikes on the financial district, Riyadh airport and Sadara Chemical in Jubail; those claims were not independently verified.

The strikes target the symbols of the kingdom's economic diversification drive. Since September, Houthi attacks have hit airports, military sites and energy infrastructure, and analysts expect the conflict to run into 2027.
Gulf markets were mostly lower on Thursday as investors weighed escalation risks and hawkish Fed minutes. Saudi stocks lost 0.4%, while Qatar and Dubai each fell 0.2%.

stories.headline: SARB Holds at 7.25% in a 4-3 Vote as Three Members Push for a Hike
stories.summary: The South African Reserve Bank left the repo rate at 7.25% on 19 Nov, but three of its seven policymakers wanted a quarter-point increase. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said the bank would not hesitate to tighten if fuel-driven inflation, which hit 5.2% in October, threatens the 3% target. The next decision is due on 28 Jan.
stories.market: Reaction was muted because the hold was largely priced in, and the rand stayed near its weakest level against the dollar this year after losing about 3% over the past month (as of 19 Nov); the split vote keeps a January hike in play for rate-sensitive banks and retailers.

body: The Monetary Policy Committee kept the repo rate at 7.25% on Thursday, leaving the prime lending rate at 10.75%. Four members voted to hold and three backed a 25-basis-point rise, a closer split than markets usually see from Pretoria. The pause follows two increases earlier in 2026.

The decision came a day after October consumer inflation jumped to 5.2% from 4.5%, the highest reading since May 2024, with core inflation edging up to 4.2%. Fuel is the main culprit: fuel inflation is running near 40%, transport makes up more than a third of overall inflation, and petrol costs almost R30 a litre against about R21 a year ago.

Kganyago described policy as moderately restrictive and said the committee agrees on the direction of travel and differs only on pace. The bank expects inflation to stay above 5% into early 2027 before easing as comparisons move past pre-war fuel prices. Its model still points to lower rates next year, but the governor stressed that each meeting will depend on the data.

The bank set out two risk scenarios. If oil reaches $130 a barrel with high refinery margins, inflation stays above 5% next year, growth slows to about 1% and roughly two more hikes would be needed. A mix of higher global bond yields, wider risk premiums and a weaker rand would produce a similar outcome.

On growth, the outlook is broadly unchanged at about 2% a year, up from just over 1% now, helped by firmer trade and retail activity. Economists flagged the expected loss of US AGOA trade benefits next year as a fresh drag, and fixed investment remains low at about 13% of GDP.
