stories.market: Egypt's main index slipped 0.2% to 51,458 on 19 Nov; with the policy rate at 20%, investors watch the 17 Dec central-bank meeting for the next steer on the pound and local debt.

stories.headline: Naira Weakens to 1,352 as Analysts Split on a CBN Cut Next Week
stories.summary: The naira traded at 1,352 per dollar on the official market on 19 Nov, down from 1,342 a week earlier, with the street rate at 1,440, and traders expect more pressure from foreign profit-taking and seasonal imports. The Central Bank of Nigeria meets on 23-24 Nov with its rate at 23%; inflation has slowed to 14.06%, the lowest since 2020, so analysts lean towards a hold or a small cut.
stories.market: A cut would narrow the gap between the 23% policy rate and inflation that has drawn foreign portfolio money, a risk for the naira and for Nigerian bond and treasury-bill yields.

body: The naira slipped on the official market this week, trading at 1,352 per dollar on Thursday against 1,342 a week before; the parallel-market rate was about 1,440. Traders told Reuters they expect further weakness next week as foreign portfolio investors take profits and importers buy dollars ahead of the festive season.
Headline inflation eased to 14.06% in October from 14.63%, the lowest since September 2020, and core inflation dropped sharply to 10.78% from 12.95%. Food inflation slowed to 19.13%.

The CBN cut its policy rate by 350bp to 23% in September but framed that move as aligning with market rates rather than the start of an easing cycle. The rate now sits about nine points above headline inflation.

Analysts surveyed by Nairametrics before the inflation data all expected a hold. After it, some see room for a 50bp cut if disinflation lasts, but none expects another large reduction, given the recent pressure on the naira.
detail.consensus: Analysts lean towards a hold at 23% or at most a small cut at the 23-24 Nov meeting.

stories.headline: Takaichi Seeks 'Stable' China Ties and Raises Japan Tobacco's Seized Assets With Putin
stories.summary: On her first trip to China as prime minister, Sanae Takaichi told reporters at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 19 November that she wants a constructive and stable relationship with Beijing; she had shaken hands with Xi Jinping twice but held no formal meeting as of that afternoon. She also spoke with Vladimir Putin for more than 30 minutes, raising a detained Japanese citizen and the treatment of Japanese firms after the Kremlin ordered the seizure of Japan Tobacco International's Russian assets this month.
stories.market: A thaw with Beijing matters for Japanese retailers, airlines and cosmetics makers hit by China's travel warnings and trade curbs since 2025; the JTI seizure is a direct hit to Japan Tobacco's Russian business.

body: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi used a news conference at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on 19 November to say she wants a constructive and stable relationship with China, calling it an important neighbour with which dialogue is needed because of outstanding issues.

It was her first trip to China since taking office and since her remarks a year ago suggesting Japan could intervene militarily if Beijing tried to take Taiwan by force. China answered those remarks with trade restrictions and a warning to its citizens against travel to Japan. As of Thursday afternoon she had shaken hands with Xi Jinping twice but had not held a formal meeting.

On the sidelines she held her first face-to-face talks with Vladimir Putin, lasting over 30 minutes. They discussed a detained Japanese national and the treatment of Japanese companies; earlier in November the Kremlin ordered the seizure of Japan Tobacco International's Russian assets, which Tokyo protested. Both sides agreed to keep channels open, including leader-level contact.

The meeting followed a Japanese protest a day earlier over suspected Russian aircraft entering its airspace, as well as protests over Putin's August visit to the disputed Kuril Islands and announced Russian missile tests nearby.

stories.headline: After Its Surprise Hike, Economists See Bank Indonesia Going Higher
stories.summary: Following Wednesday's 25bp hike to 6%, which Governor Destry Damayanti called pre-emptive ahead of a possible Fed increase, local economists now pencil in more tightening: Bank Danamon sees room for a second move next month and Permata Bank expects the rate to end 2027 at 6.5%. The rupiah closed at 18,232 per dollar on 18 November, little changed from about 18,250 before the decision.
stories.market: The modest rupiah bounce shows how far rate differentials have to go; Danamon expects the 10-year government bond yield to ease to about 7.4% by year-end from 7.6% on 18 November.

body: Bank Indonesia raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 6% on Wednesday 18 November. Governor Destry Damayanti described the move as pre-emptive, aimed at keeping Indonesian assets attractive and drawing inflows before a possible US rate increase.

The rupiah had hit fresh record lows as the dollar firmed on Fed-hike expectations. It traded around 18,250 per dollar before the announcement and closed the spot session at 18,232. Headline inflation of 3.23% sits near the top of the 1.5-3.5% target band, and Deputy Governor Aida Budiman said the hike was also meant to anchor inflation as oil prices and the weak currency feed imported inflation.

Economists quoted on 20 November see more to come. Bank Danamon's Irman Faiz said growth of 5.45% in the first nine months leaves room for another pre-emptive hike next month; Permata Bank's Faisal Rachman forecast the policy rate ending 2027 at 6.5%.
detail.consensus: Local economists quoted expect at least one more hike, with Permata forecasting 6.5% by end-2027.

stories.headline: Sri Lanka Surprises With a Rate Hike to 9% as Inflation Hits 8.3%
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka raised its overnight policy rate by 25 basis points to 9.00% on 20 November, after its board met on 19 November; markets had expected no change. It also lifted the statutory reserve ratio by one point to 3.00% from 9 December, citing October inflation of 8.3% and still-strong private credit growth.
stories.market: The move tightens rupee liquidity and is a negative for Colombo-listed banks' margins in the near term; the rupee closed at about 332.75 per dollar on 19 November, before the decision.

body: Sri Lanka's central bank raised the Overnight Policy Rate by a quarter point to 9.00% in a decision announced on Friday 20 November, following a Monetary Policy Board meeting on 19 November. Local reporting described the move as a surprise: markets had priced an unchanged stance.

The bank paired the hike with a one-percentage-point increase in the Statutory Reserve Ratio to 3.00%, effective from the reserve maintenance period that begins on 9 December 2026. Raising the SRR drains rupee liquidity from the banking system on top of the higher policy rate.

The bank tied the decision to a Middle East conflict that has lasted longer than expected, high global energy and food prices, likely second-round effects from earlier energy price rises and higher one-year-ahead inflation expectations. It also flagged that its own foreign-exchange purchases have added rupee liquidity that could slow the cooling of credit growth.

Headline inflation rose to 8.3% year on year in October, with core inflation also climbing, well above the bank's 5% target. The bank said it expects inflation to return to target in the second half of 2027 and pointed to private-sector credit growth that has slowed but remains high.

The rupee has weakened gradually but the bank described it as broadly stable. It closed at 332.75/85 per dollar on 19 November against 332.73/80 a day earlier; government bond yields were flat on 19 November, before the announcement.
detail.consensus: Markets had expected the central bank to hold its policy rate unchanged.
